body: Founded 1995 by ex-VC Mark Leonard; IPO on TSX May 2006 (~C$17.50 [unverified]). Model: buy hundreds of small vertical-market software (VMS) firms at low multiples with strict hurdle rates, keep them decentralised, reinvest all cash flow; Leonard's letters reported ROIC and organic growth candidly and set the playbook (later spun-offs Topicus, Lumine). Peak ~C$5,000-5,300 (2025) [unverified] ≈ 300x + dividends. Split: almost entirely FCF/share growth; P/E/FCF multiple also rose from ~10-15x to ~30x+ [approx]. Drawdowns: ~-35-40% in 2008 [unverified]; then the big one: Sept 25 2025 Leonard resigned for health reasons (Mark Miller president), shares closed the week -17% days after an investor call on AI worries; National Bank downgraded; AI-disruption fear hit all SaaS/VMS; by Feb 2026 ~-51% from highs, 52-week low ~C$2,624 (Jan 2026), ~16-17x forward earnings by mid-2026. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2006-2012: shareholder letters showing high returns on many small, boring acquisitions, a growing count of deals per year, and owner-operator incentives (managers required to buy shares with bonus). Who caught it: early backers OMERS/Ontario pension funds; a cult following of quality investors [names unverified]. LESSON: capital-allocation compounders depend on the allocator and on the redeployment runway; key-person exit + a new technology threat can halve even a 300x stock without any fundamental miss yet.

data.early_signals: letters showing high ROIC on small VMS deals; owner incentives
data.lesson: key-person + runway risk in serial acquirers

title: Constellation Software 2006-2025: serial VMS acquirer ~300x, then -50%
